areas.description: Settings related to thermostat, multi-room and temperature control. The radiators are in the same room as the inside sensor and the rooms have their own target temperatures separate from the system.
areas.title: Areas

automatic_gains.description:
This feature adjusts the control parameters of your heating system dynamically, optimizing temperature control for better comfort and energy efficiency. Enabling this option allows SAT to continuously adapt and fine-tune the heating settings based on the environmental conditions. This helps maintain a stable and comfortable environment without manual intervention.

Note: If you choose not to enable automatic gains, you will need to manually enter the PID values for precise temperature control. Please ensure that you have accurate PID values for your specific heating system to achieve optimal performance.
automatic_gains.title: Automatic Gains

calibrate_system.description:
Optimize your heating system by automatically determining the optimal PID values for your setup. When selecting Automatic Gains, please note that the system will go through a calibration process that may take approximately 20 minutes to complete.

Automatic Gains is recommended for most users as it simplifies the setup process and ensures optimal performance. However, if you're familiar with PID control and prefer to manually set the values, you can choose to skip Automatic Gains.

Please note that choosing to skip Automatic Gains requires a good understanding of PID control and may require additional manual adjustments to achieve optimal performance.

menu_options.calibrate: Calibrate and determine your overshoot protection value (approx. 20 min).
menu_options.overshoot_protection: Manually enter the overshoot protection value.

calibrate_system.title: Calibrate System

calibrated.description:
The calibration process has completed successfully.

Congratulations! Your Smart Autotune Thermostat (SAT) has been calibrated to optimize the heating performance of your system. During the calibration process, SAT carefully analyzed the heating characteristics and determined the appropriate overshoot protection value to ensure precise temperature control.

Overshoot Protection Value: {minimum_setpoint} °C

This value represents the maximum amount of overshoot allowed during the heating process. SAT will actively monitor and adjust the heating to prevent excessive overshooting, maintaining a comfortable and efficient heating experience in your home.

Please note that the overshoot protection value may vary depending on the specific characteristics of your heating system and environmental factors. It has been fine-tuned to provide optimal performance based on the calibration results.
calibrated.title: Calibration Completed

overshoot_protection.description:
By providing the overshoot protection value, SAT will adjust the control parameters accordingly to maintain a stable and comfortable heating environment. This manual configuration allows you to fine-tune the system based on your specific setup.

Note: If you are unsure about the overshoot protection value or have not performed the calibration process, it is recommended to cancel the configuration and go through the calibration process to let SAT automatically determine the value for optimal performance.

serial.description:
To establish a connection with the OpenTherm Gateway using a socket connection, please provide the following details. In the Name field, enter a name for the gateway that will help you identify it within your system.

Specify the network address of the OpenTherm Gateway in the Device field. This could be in the format of "{example_device}", where "otgw.local" is the hostname or IP address of the gateway and "25238" is the port number.

These settings are essential for establishing communication and integration with your OpenTherm Gateway through the socket connection. Ensure that the provided details are accurate to ensure proper functionality.
serial.title: OpenTherm Gateway ( SERIAL )

simulator.description:
This gateway allows you to simulate a boiler for testing and demonstration purposes. Please provide the following information to configure the simulator.

Note: The Simulator Gateway is intended for testing and demonstration purposes only and should not be used in production environments.
simulator.title: Simulated Gateway ( ADVANCED )

switch.description:
Please fill in the following details to set up the switch. Enter a name for the switch in the Name field, which will help you identify it within your system. Choose the appropriate entity to use for your switch from the provided options.

In the Temperature Setting field, specify the desired target temperature for your heating system. If you are using a hot water boiler, fill in the Boiler Temperature Setting with the appropriate value. For electric heating systems, enter the value 100.

These settings are essential for precise temperature control and ensuring optimal performance of your heating system. Providing the correct Temperature Setting allows for accurate regulation and helps achieve a comfortable and energy-efficient environment in your home.
switch.title: PID Thermostat with PWM ( ON/OFF )

data_description.automatic_gains_value: The value used for automatic gains in the PID controller.
data_description.derivative: The derivative term (kD) in the PID controller, responsible for mitigating overshooting.
data_description.derivative_time_weight: A parameter to adjust the influence of the derivative term over time, particularly useful for reducing undershoot during the warm-up phase when the heating curve coefficient is correctly set.
data_description.duty_cycle: The maximum duty cycle for Pulse Width Modulation (PWM), controlling the boiler's on-off cycles.
data_description.heating_curve_coefficient: The coefficient used to adjust the heating curve.
data_description.integral: The integral term (kI) in the PID controller, responsible for reducing steady-state error.
data_description.maximum_setpoint: The optimal temperature for efficient boiler operation.
data_description.proportional: The proportional term (kP) in the PID controller, responsible for the immediate response to errors.
data_description.window_sensors: Contact Sensors that trigger the system to react when a window or door is open for a period of time.
data_description.minimum_setpoint: Lowest flow temperature the boiler holds at minimum modulation.

data.push_setpoint_to_thermostat: Synchronize with thermostat attached to the boiler
data.sync_climates_with_preset: Synchronize climates with preset (sleep / away / activity)

presets.description: Predefined temperature settings for different scenarios or activities.
presets.title: Presets

data.window_minimum_open_time: Minimum time for window to be open
data.default_hvac_mode: Mode when nothing can be restored

data_description.cycles_per_hour: The maximum amount of duty cycles per hour.
data_description.automatic_duty_cycle: Enable or disable automatic duty cycle for Pulse Width Modulation (PWM).
data_description.overshoot_protection: Enable overshoot protection with Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) to prevent boiler temperature overshooting.
data_description.sensor_max_value_age: The maximum age of the temperature sensor value before considering it as a stall.
data_description.window_minimum_open_time: The minimum time a window must be open before the system reacts.
data_description.default_hvac_mode: HVAC mode used on the first start, or when no saved state is available.

data.gas_energy_content: Heat per cubic metre of gas
data.pwm_short_burns_threshold: Cut-short burns before ending the PWM on-phase
data.keep_heating_in_pwm_off: Keep heating enabled between PWM on-phases
data.window_detection: Detect open windows from the temperature

data_description.climate_valve_offset: Offset to adjust the opening degree of the climate valve.
data_description.dynamic_minimum_setpoint: Activates the dynamic setpoint adjustment based on the boiler's return temperature, which also helps identify if any valves are closed.
data_description.maximum_consumption: The maximum gas consumption when the boiler is active.
data_description.maximum_relative_modulation: Representing the highest modulation level for an efficient heating system.
data_description.minimum_consumption: The minimum gas consumption when the boiler is active.
data_description.sample_time: The minimum time interval between updates to the PID controller.
data_description.target_temperature_step: Adjust the target temperature step for fine-tuning comfort levels.
data_description.thermal_comfort: Enable the use of the Simmer Index for thermal comfort adjustment.
data_description.calibration_flame_timeout: How long the overshoot protection calibration waits for the burner to light.
data_description.calibration_plateau_timeout: How long the overshoot protection calibration heats while waiting for a stable flow temperature.
data_description.gas_energy_content: Heat the boiler gets from one cubic metre of gas, in kWh/m³: about 10.2 for natural gas, 24 for propane. Used for the gas, heat and water flow estimates.
data_description.pwm_short_burns_threshold: How many burns the boiler may cut short in one PWM on-phase before SAT ends the on-phase early. 1 allows a single burn per on-phase (default 2).
data_description.boiler_anti_cycling_time: The boiler's own wait before it relights (anti-cycling). SAT waits this long plus a minute before reporting the flame as stuck off, and calibration waits at least this long plus two minutes for the burner to light. 0 keeps the defaults.
data_description.learn_overshoot_protection: Start from the calibrated value and adjust it during normal operation: up when the boiler stops PWM burns by overheating or cannot light, down when long burns level off below the setpoint. Calibrating again or changing the value starts over.
data_description.valve_opening_time: How long the valve actuators of the radiator and room thermostats take to open. When a thermostat starts asking for heat and no other one has asked for longer, SAT waits this long before lighting the boiler. 0 lights it at once.
data_description.warm_up_modulation: For a burner whose flame goes out at its minimum power while the system water is still cold. In the first 10 minutes of a heating burn, while the return is below 33 °C, SAT lets the boiler modulate up to this share instead of holding it at its minimum; then the minimum applies again. 0 turns it off.
data_description.keep_heating_in_pwm_off: Leaves central heating enabled at the minimum setpoint in PWM off-phases instead of switching it off. The boiler stays in heating mode, so its pump keeps circulating through the floor and a combi boiler with a hot water cylinder does not swing its diverter valve to the cylinder and cool it with the pump overrun. If the boiler lights during an off-phase anyway, SAT switches heating off between on-phases again for an hour.
data_description.heat_budget_mode: For slow emitters such as screed underfloor heating. SAT learns how much heat the house loses per degree (from the burner time and the indoor and outdoor temperatures over each day) and, once it knows, burns the heat the next period needs in one block at minimum power, carrying over heat that hot water or a boiler cut-out kept from being delivered. Learn only (shadow) learns and shows its plan in the climate attributes without controlling. Until it has learned (about 36 hours) the normal PWM controls.
data_description.heat_budget_period: How often the heat budget burns one block. Longer periods mean fewer, longer burns; the screed evens out the room temperature.
data_description.heat_budget_minimum_burn: The shortest block worth lighting the burner for. Less heat than this is carried into the next period.
data_description.heat_loss_coefficient: Heat the house loses per degree between inside and outside, in W/K. 0 learns it.
data_description.weather_forecast_entity_id: A weather entity with an hourly forecast. The heat budget plans with the temperature of the next three hours and, when the forecast has cloud cover, learns how much the sun heats the house.
data_description.comfort_schedule_entity_id: A schedule helper that is on when the house should be at the target temperature. Outside it the heat budget lowers the target by the setback, starts the recovery early enough to be warm when the schedule turns on (learned from earlier recoveries) and stops an hour early because the screed keeps heating.
data_description.setback_temperature: How much lower the heat budget keeps the house outside the comfort schedule. With screed floors small setbacks save little.
data_description.warm_weather_shutdown_temperature: Central heating switches off while the outside temperature averaged over a day is at or above this, and back on 2 °C below it (a forecast keeps it off when warm weather returns soon). Hot water keeps working. 0 keeps heating on.
data_description.hot_water_schedule_entity_id: A schedule helper that is on in the hours hot water is used. Outside them the eco temperature applies.
data_description.hot_water_comfort_temperature: The cylinder temperature SAT sends to the boiler; 0 leaves the hot water to the boiler.
data_description.hot_water_eco_temperature: The cylinder temperature outside the schedule's hours; 0 uses the hot water temperature all day.
data_description.legionella_day: Once a week the cylinder is held at 60 °C for an hour.
data_description.legionella_time: When the weekly boost starts, best in the night.
data_description.presence_entity_ids: People, device trackers, zones or groups. When nobody has been home for 30 minutes SAT switches to the Away preset, and back when someone returns.
data_description.proximity_entity_id: A distance sensor (Proximity integration). Within the return distance the house counts as occupied again, so a slow floor starts warming early.
data_description.return_distance: How close someone must be for the heating to come back; 0 waits until they are home.
data_description.window_detection: Without contact sensors: a room temperature drop of 0.8 °C within 10 minutes or 0.3 °C within 30 minutes switches to the Activity preset until the room stops cooling (2 hours at most). Needs a sensor that reports tenths of a degree.
data_description.screed_maximum_temperature: Flow water above this for 3 minutes in space heating raises a repair issue. Underfloor heating only; 0 turns it off.
data_description.last_service_date: A repair issue reminds you when the next service is due.
data_description.gas_price: Including distribution, in your currency. Adds an estimated gas cost sensor; 0 turns it off.
data_description.condensing_boiler: For the efficiency estimate of a boiler that does not report its flue gas temperature: a condensing boiler runs its flue a few kelvin above the return water. Turn off for an older non-condensing boiler, which then gets no estimate without a flue gas sensor.

reset_integral.name: Reset Integral
reset_integral.description: This service resets the integrating part of the PID controller for the specified climate entity. This may be useful if the integral value has become too large or if the PID controller's performance has degraded.

measure_loops.name: Measure loops
measure_loops.description: Measures the water flow of each heating loop by turning the room thermostats off and opening them one at a time while the burner runs at minimum power. Takes about 15 minutes per room; the thermostats are put back afterwards and the result comes as a notification.

Setting up {title} failed and Home Assistant keeps retrying: {error}

While it retries, the room thermostat attached to the boiler is in control.

low_water_pressure.title: {title}: low water pressure
low_water_pressure.description: The heating system pressure is {pressure} bar. Top the system up to about 1.2–1.5 bar (cold) and check for leaks or a flat expansion vessel if it keeps dropping. This issue clears itself above 0.9 bar.

boiler_fault.title: {title}: the boiler reports a fault
boiler_fault.description: The boiler reports a fault (manufacturer code {code}). Check the boiler display and its manual. This issue clears itself when the boiler no longer reports the fault.

heat_exchanger_fouling.title: {title}: the heat exchanger may need cleaning
heat_exchanger_fouling.description: In settled heating burns the flue gas has been about {gap} K warmer than the return water over the last day. A clean condensing boiler stays within a few kelvin, so the heat exchanger or the burner may need a service.

pressure_falling.title: {title}: water pressure keeps falling
pressure_falling.description: The water pressure of {title} fell by {per_week} bar a week over the last days, to {pressure} bar. Look for a leak or a failing expansion vessel before the boiler locks out.

screed_overheat.title: {title}: flow water too hot for the floor
screed_overheat.description: {title} sent {flow} °C to the floor for minutes, above the {limit} °C limit. Check the boiler's maximum heating temperature.

low_water_flow.title: {title}: too little water through the heating
low_water_flow.description: The flow of {title} ran {spread} K warmer than the return in settled burns. Too little water moves: check the loops, the filter and for air in the system.

boiler_service_due.title: {title}: boiler service due
boiler_service_due.description: The service of {title} was due on {due}.

gas_use_increased.title: {title}: gas use went up
gas_use_increased.description: {title} used {percent} % more gas per degree day last week than in the weeks before. Look for an open window, a closed loop or a boiler problem.
